metas.name: 1 Insulator Pole
metas.note: • Poles with only one insulator on the crossbar can be found from south on the peninsula from Ranong and Chumphon.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: 2 Insulators Pole
metas.note: • Poles with two insulators on the crossbar can be found in the rest of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: 7 Ridge Insulators
metas.note:
• Insulators with 7 or more ridges are found in the southern half of the peninsula, as well as highways in Chiang Rai and Phayao.

--- NOTE:

  • In the north, you may still find 5 or 6 ridges on insulators, as these are the standard amount throughout the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Areca Palms
metas.note: • Areca palms are mainly found across the peninsula, but are especially common around Ranong.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Cassava
metas.note:
• Cassava is a bush-like plant with digitate leaves.
  • It can be found throughout most of Thailand, but is considerably more common in the central and northeastern plains.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Chilean Style Pole
metas.note:
• Regular poles with a Chilean style indent are found around Bangkok.

--- NOTE:

  • Larger and thicker poles with indents are found on highways all throughout the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Corn
metas.note: • Corn is most commonly found in the north and central regions of Thailand.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Corrugated Metal Roofs
metas.note: • Gray corrugated metal roofs are most commonly found in the north and south of the country, but can occasionally be found throughout the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Dense Eucalyptus Plantations
metas.note:
• Eucalyptus plantations are most common around Sa Kaeo.

--- NOTE:

  • Eucalyptus can be found in smaller quantities, such as lining the road, in different areas.
  • This tip is exclusively about dense plantations.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Dry Season Rice
metas.note:
• Rice cultivated during the dry season is most common in the central plains.
  • The dry season in Thailand can typically be recognized by a haze in the sky due to wildfires.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Durian Plantations
metas.note:
• Durian plantations are most common around Chanthaburi, but can be found around the peninsula and other areas.
  • When they are young, they can be identified by their cone-shaped appearance.
  • When fully grown, durian trees can be identified by their dark bark, branches that nearly reach the ground, and oblong leaves with pointed tips.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Exposed Rock
metas.note: • Steep mountains with a lot of exposed rock are most commonly found in the west and on the peninsula.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Flat & Dry Landscape
metas.note:
• Thailand has two regions that are relatively flat and dry compared to other areas.
  • One north of Bangkok, the other more east.

--- NOTE:

  • The eastern area feels sometimes a bit drier than the area north of Bangkok.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Fruit Plantations
metas.note: • The most extensive fruit plantations can be found in the valley between Chiang Mai and Lamphun as well as eastern Sa Kaeo and Chanthaburi.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Garden Croton Plant
metas.note:
• Garden croton is a decorative plant recognised by its yellow, orange and red leaves.
  • It is most common around Ranong and other coastal provinces.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Gravel Road
metas.note: • Gravel roads can be found all throughout Thailand, but are most common in the darkly highlighted areas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Low & Forested Mountains
metas.note: • Low, smooth and forested mountains can be found in the centre-north of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Palm Oil Plantations
metas.note:
• Over 90% of the palm oil in Thailand is produced in the south.
  • This means that palm plantations are most often seen in southern Thailand.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Palmyra Palms
metas.note:
• Large numbers of palmyra palms are typically found near the eastern coast of the peninsula, specifically just south of Bangkok as well as in the far south.

--- NOTE:

  • Lone or small clusters of palmyra palms can be found all throughout the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Pineapple Plantations
metas.note: • Pineapple plantations are most commonly found southeast and southwest of Bangkok.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Red Soil
metas.note: • Red soil is most common in the northeast of Thailand, but can be seen throughout the entire country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Rice
metas.note: • A majority of Thailand’s rice cultivation occurs within the highlighted area.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Rubber Wood
metas.note:
• Rubber wood plantations are typically seen in Thailand.
  • Most of them are located in the south.
  • You can recognize them by the small, black taps on the bottom of the tree's trunk.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Short Coconut Palms
metas.note: • Dense plantations of short or medium sized coconut palms are most commonly found west of Bangkok.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Sugar Cane
metas.note: • Sugar cane is mostly grown in central and eastern Thailand.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Tall Coconut Palms
metas.note:
• Slightly less dense plantations of tall coconut palms are most common in Prachuap Khiri Khan.

--- NOTE:

  • The entire peninsula will have many coconut palms, this tip only refers to plantations.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Tall Mountains
metas.note:
• Tall mountains are most often seen in northwestern Thailand.

--- NOTE:

  • Some parts of the southern peninsular part are also mountainous.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Teak Trees
metas.note:
• Teak trees are most commonly found in high densities in the north.
  • It can be recognized by its large leaves and yellow flowers.

--- NOTE:

  • Teak trees are often used for decoration along highways.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Tenasserim Pines
metas.note: • Pine trees, specifically tenasserim pines, are more or less exclusive to the north and northwest of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Wet Season Rice
metas.note: During the wet season, the majority of rice cultivation occurs in the eastern plains.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Wind Turbines
metas.note: • Wind turbines are most often found on the western side of Chaiyaphum and Nakhon Ratchasima as well as the eastern coast of Songkhla and Nakhon Si Thammarat.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.
